process_note: The sfnl-prompt-master skill is not available to this subagent, so the hunt ran on its definition alone.
conviction_note: Sales are already out (+2.6%, comps +0.6%), so the print turns on margin and on what management says about November on the 10:00 ET call. My arithmetic from the Q2 cost run-rate gives EPS of about $0.86, against a disputed bar of $0.84-0.92. That is a small negative lean on the quarter. It is roughly offset by a stock sold down 11% in 20 days, sitting below the lone UBS $45 target, with 9 days to cover. p_up is 47 on an abs_move of 5.5: the 13.7% option-implied move rests on a chain with a 47% ATM spread and is not usable, and the name's own median reaction is 2.4% with a max of 9.1%. The findings sum (-0.2) and the scaled number (-0.33) agree in sign and are both near zero.
bar: Disputed, so every finding is capped small. EPS $0.88, revenue $326.3m, EBIT $56.05m (down 8.5% y/y) per an iTiger preview dated 2026-11-13 (https://www.itiger.com/news/1134066982). A single-analyst next-quarter consensus of $0.84 per AAII (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/535761-what-you-need-to-know-about-the-buckle-incs-q3-earnings, 2026-11-19, ambiguous period). Search snippets also mention $0.92 with no verifiable page. Prior-year Q3 was diluted EPS $0.96, operating margin 19.0%, gross margin 48.0% (https://www.rttnews.com/3597679/buckle-inc-bottom-line-rises-in-q3-beats-estimates.aspx). Revenue is no longer a bar: $329.2m was pre-released on 2026-11-05 (https://finviz.com/news/416668/the-buckle-inc-reports-october-2026-net-sales). The company gives no guidance.
positioning_check: Short interest per equibles (FINRA data, https://equibles.com/stocks/bke/short-interest): 3,593,752 shares on the 2026-10-30 settlement, 9.12 days to cover, about 7.0% of 51.5m shares outstanding. The 2026-10-15 settlement was 3,739,326 shares at 9.35 days. The trend is flat to slightly covering. The float is materially smaller than shares outstanding because of insider holdings (not sourced here), so the short is a higher share of float. 25-delta skew is +3.16 vol points (downside paid, a mild lean), but the chain is thin (1,511 OI, ATM spread 47% of mid) and put/call OI is 0.29. A crowded-ish short on high days-to-cover argues for shrinking the negatives.

expectations.price_path: Sealed baseline: 5-day -4.04%, 20-day -11.19%, 26.6% below the 52-week high and 6.3% above the 52-week low. The finviz news list shows -7.33% beside the 2026-11-05 October sales release (https://finviz.com/news/416668/the-buckle-inc-reports-october-2026-net-sales). The official close was $41.96, -5.43%, on 2026-11-06 (https://markets.financialcontent.com/streetinsider/quote?Symbol=BKE). Sector ETF comparison not found.
expectations.vs_targets: Spot $42.17 against a UBS Neutral target cut to $45 (iTiger, 2026-11-13, https://www.itiger.com/news/1134066982). Investing.com shows 2 analysts with a $46 mean and $46 high (https://ca.investing.com/equities/the-buckle-inc-consensus-estimates, undated). Spot is about 6-8% below the targets.
expectations.whisper_or_buyside_bar: not found. The only 'street needs' text is UBS expecting Q3 gross-margin contraction and slower online traffic (iTiger, 2026-11-13).
expectations.last_print: Q2 (2026-08-21): diluted EPS $0.87 vs $0.81 consensus. Gross margin was +40bp, helped by a 65bp tariff refund, and operating margin was -100bp. The stock rose +2.74% (baseline; https://finviz.com/news/384450/the-buckle-inc-reports-second-quarter-net-income). Q1 (2026-05-29): gross margin -50bp on tariffs and occupancy, and the stock fell -9.13% (baseline).
expectations.short_interest_trend: 2026-10-15: 3,739,326 shares, 9.35 days to cover. 2026-10-30: 3,593,752 shares, 9.12 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/bke/short-interest).
expectations.real_bar: With sales known and decelerating (October comps -0.5%), the stock rises if gross margin holds near last year's 48.0% without the refund, SG&A deleverage is no worse than Q2's +140bp, and the November commentary on the call is not negative.

next_guide.street_full_year: not found (AAII, 2026-11-19, says the current-year EPS estimate fell 2.2% in the last month)
next_guide.company_current_guide: none: management said on the Q2 call that it does not provide sales or earnings guidance (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/BKE/Q22026)
next_guide.basis: Buckle gives no guidance, so the forward signal is the call's quarter-to-date November commentary. The monthly comps trajectory (Aug +1.6%, Sep +0.5%, Oct -0.5%) and Boot Barn's 0.4% October comp point to a soft tone.

findings.finding: Q2's gross-margin help from tariff refunds does not recur. Merchandise margin was +110bp in Q2, of which 65bp came from tariff refunds; management said 'all of the refunds that we expect to receive were received' and 'most of it has been recognized', with only a small residual in Q3. Q3 gross margin therefore has to beat last year's 48.0% without that 65bp. Consensus EBIT of $56.05m (-8.5% y/y) already assumes contraction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin is the line this name trades on. Q1 gross margin -50bp: -9.13%. Q2 gross margin +40bp, flattered by the refund, with an EPS beat: +2.74%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. UBS and the iTiger preview both expect gross-margin contraction, and consensus EPS is -8.85% y/y. What may not be fully priced is that the comparison is against a refund-flattered Q2: if the street extrapolated Q2's +40bp, the Q3 gross-margin print reads worse than trend.
findings.independence: The UBS view of Q3 gross-margin contraction (https://www.itiger.com/news/1134066982) is a different source pointing the same way.

findings.finding: Operating cost deleverage on weaker comps. In Q2, comps of +2.1% still produced +140bp of SG&A deleverage (marketing +45bp, store labor +35bp, health insurance +30bp, supplies +20bp) and +70bp of buying, distribution and occupancy deleverage. Q3 comps were only +0.6% on 451 stores vs 442 a year earlier. Applying Q2's ~9.6% SG&A dollar growth to Q3 gives SG&A of about 31.0% of sales. With flat-to-down gross margin that is EBIT of about $55m vs $56.05m consensus and EPS of about $0.86 vs $0.88.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's operating-margin decline of -100bp was overlooked on an EPS beat (+2.74%). Q1's margin pressure was sold (-9.13%).
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus already embeds an EBIT decline of about 8.5%. My estimate is only about $1m of EBIT below it, inside the noise of a disputed bar. If it were fully priced, consensus would sit at about $0.86, not $0.88-0.92.
findings.independence: The SG&A breakdown comes from the Q2 call (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/BKE/Q22026), which shares a quarter with the release. Store count (451 vs 442) is from the 2026-11-05 sales release. Both rest on the Q2 reporting, so they count once.

findings.finding: Comps decelerated through Q3 in the company's own monthly releases: August +1.6% (net sales +3.6%), September +0.5% (+2.2%), October -0.5% (+1.8%). These are against tough prior-year compares (September 2025 comps were +6.9%). Exiting the quarter negative makes the 10:00 ET call's November/holiday quarter-to-date commentary the main forward signal, since there is no guidance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The October sales release on 2026-11-05 was followed by about -7% (finviz news list -7.33%; official close -5.43% on 2026-11-06), so the market reacts to monthly comps.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The stock fell about 7% on the release and is -11% over 20 days. The residual is that November commentary on the call is new information and the trajectory points to a soft read. If it were fully priced, the stock would not have partly rebounded to about $44 by 2026-11-12 before fading back to $42.
findings.independence: September: https://www.rttnews.com/3697505/buckle-september-sales-rise-2-2.aspx. August: https://www.financialcontent.com/article/bizwire-2026-9-3-the-buckle-inc-reports-august-2026-net-sales. All are company releases, so they count as one series.

findings.finding: Boot Barn's fiscal Q2 (quarter to 2026-09-26, reported late October 2026) showed same-store sales slowing to +1.4%, preliminary October comps of +0.4%, and a cut to the full-year comp guide from 2-4% to 0.8-2%. That matches Buckle's October deceleration in an overlapping region and customer.
findings.link: Overlapping customer and region: both are mid-America and western-skewed specialty apparel and footwear chains, and Buckle sells western brands (e.g., Ariat, Kimes Ranch per its brand list, not sourced here). There are no shared revenue figures, so the link is qualitative.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is public since late October and Buckle's own October comp has since been released. It is filed as corroboration of a soft November tone.
findings.independence: Boot Barn 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001610250/000110465926119615/boot-ex99d1.htm. This is independent of Buckle's own releases.

findings.finding: Expectations are already lowered going into the print. The stock is -11.2% over 20 days and -4.0% over 5 days, 26.6% below its 52-week high and only 6.3% above its 52-week low, about 6-8% below the lone UBS Neutral target ($45, cut 2026-11-13). Consensus EPS of $0.88 is already down 8.85% y/y and full-year estimates fell 2.2% in the last month. An in-line margin print clears a bar the price has already marked down.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last print, Q2: a $0.87 vs $0.81 beat after a weak tape bought +2.74%. Q4 FY25 (2026-03-13): -0.75%. Q3 FY25 (2025-11-21): a 1c beat, -1.29%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. The question is whether the drawdown overshoots a ~2% EPS shortfall. If the market expected a clean in-line print, the stock would not be near its 52-week low on a quarter whose sales came in above the $326m consensus.
findings.independence: The sealed baseline tape and https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/535761-what-you-need-to-know-about-the-buckle-incs-q3-earnings (estimate revisions) are different sources pointing the same way.

findings.finding: Short interest is about 3.6m shares (about 7% of shares outstanding and more of the insider-reduced float) with 9.1 days to cover on about 394k average daily volume (2026-10-30 settlement). On a thin-volume name, any relief on margin meets a short that needs over a week of volume to cover.
findings.why_not_priced: Days to cover is a convexity mechanism, not a level the price reflects. Mild covering since September (3.93m to 3.59m shares) shows shorts are not pressing into the print.
findings.independence: The FINRA short-interest figures are reproduced by equibles. There is no second independent source.

findings.finding: Q2 SG&A included a 35bp lower incentive and equity compensation accrual. With the year's earnings running below last year (consensus EPS -8.85% y/y in Q3), the incentive accrual is likely to stay lower in Q3, a partial offset to deleverage that is not obvious from sales.
findings.why_not_priced: Inference from the call. Previews mention only cost pressure. If the street modelled it, consensus EBIT would not be as low as -8.5% y/y on +2.6% sales.
findings.independence: Same document as the SG&A breakdown in the deleverage finding: read together, they count once.

findings.finding: Other income should be lower year on year. Q3 FY25 other income was about $3.6m (derived: net income $48.7m at a 24.5% tax rate less $60.9m operating income). Q2 FY26 was $3.0m after a $3.35/share (~$172m) dividend paid in January 2026 cut cash and investments to $322.9m from $349.6m a year earlier. That is about -$0.01 of EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: not measured; below the operating line
findings.why_not_priced: Small and mechanical. It is likely already in models.

findings.finding: Inventory was $161.4m at 2026-08-01, +13.3% y/y against Q2 sales +4.6%. Q3 comps then slowed to +0.6% (October -0.5%), which raises markdown risk to merchandise margin in Q3 and Q4. The build is partly explained by new stores (451 vs 442) and back-to-school timing.
findings.why_not_priced: It is in the Q2 balance sheet but absent from previews, which cite freight and occupancy rather than markdowns. If priced, previews would name clearance risk.
findings.independence: None. Store growth (2026-11-05 release) partly argues against it, which is why it is sized small.

outside_window.finding: Special dividend decision: Buckle declared its $3.00 special at the board meeting of 2025-12-08 (announced 2025-12-09), not with Q3 results. With cash and investments at $322.9m in August 2026, a December 2026 special is plausible but dated after the window.
November 2026 monthly sales release (early December) gives the hard November comp figure.

searched_and_found_nothing: mid-quarter statements: no conference or investor-day remarks found after the 2026-08-21 call; the only intra-quarter statements are the company's monthly sales releases (2026-09-03, ~2026-10-08, 2026-11-05), filed as a finding
teen/denim apparel peers reporting the Aug-Oct 2026 quarter before 2026-11-20 (AEO, ANF, URBN, ZUMZ, Tilly's report later): none found
whisper number or buy-side bar: not found
Q3 FY26 street next-quarter (Q4) and full-year EPS figures: not found
Q2 FY26 10-Q text (EDGAR browse timed out); used the release and call transcript instead
sector ETF relative performance over the 5d/20d window: not searched beyond the baseline

rejected_candidates.candidate: Consensus EPS of $0.92 and revenue $333.6m quoted by search snippets
rejected_candidates.detail: Appears only in a search summary; no fetched page confirmed the figure or its date, so it is recorded in `bar` as disputed rather than filed.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Option-implied event move of 13.67% as the scale
rejected_candidates.detail: The baseline itself warns the ATM spread is 47% of mid (indicative only). The 7-print reaction history (median 2.4%, max 9.1%) is used for scale instead.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Levi Strauss Q3 2026: US revenue -1%, US DTC -1%, raised FY EPS guide
rejected_candidates.detail: Overlaps the Boot Barn peer finding as a generic US denim-demand read. The link to Buckle (Levi's is not a core Buckle brand) is unstated, and the quarter ended 2026-08-30, so it is weaker than Boot Barn.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Q1 FY26 $19.1m interchange litigation settlement in SG&A
rejected_candidates.detail: A Q1 item that does not recur in Q3. It explains why year-to-date operating income is inflated, but it has no bearing on the Q3 print.

baseline_tension: The small negative quarter read agrees with the mild put skew (+3.16), but the 20-day run-up of -11% and 9 days to cover cut against it. That leaves a near-zero net and p_up at 47.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar disputed, $0.84 / $0.88 / ~$0.92): all findings capped small; the tariff and deleverage findings cut from -0.5 to -0.3 and -0.4, p_up moved from 45 to 47.
Lessons 6 and 1 (landing inside what consensus already models): the monthly-comps finding cut from -0.8 to -0.6, since the stock already fell ~7% on the October release.
Lesson 7 (crowded short, 9 days to cover): the inventory negative cut from -0.5 to -0.3, and the peer read and other negatives kept small.
Lesson 2 (one-off below operating income): the other-income finding cut from -0.2 to -0.1.
Lesson 8 (thin coverage, 1-2 analysts): abs_move raised from 5.0 to 5.5.
Expectations and positioning positives left unchanged.
